body.long:
Deepti on Niki Prasad: 'It didn't seem at all like she was making her debut'
Despite India slipping to 19 for 4 in the first T20I against Zimbabwe, Deepti backed the batters' aggressive approach
Cricinfo staffPublished: Oct 17, 2026, 3:36 AM (8 hrs ago)
That the hosts eventually won the first T20I in Raipur comfortably, with four wickets and 26 balls in hand, was down to an 82-run partnership for the fifth wicket between Deepti Sharma and Niki Prasad. Senior pro Deepti scored 49 off 37 balls, and Prasad, making her India debut, an unbeaten 39 off 35.
"Niki played really well," Deepti said in her post-match press conference. "Honestly, it didn't seem at all like she was making her debut. It felt like she had played quite a few matches in the past, for the country.
"This confidence from a youngster is remarkable - you're building a partnership when the team needs it, winning the match from a tough situation. I'm sure she'll take a lot of confidence from this match."
Even though the partnership began in tense circumstances, Deepti said there was no sense of panic in India's dressing room.
